questions.text:
Assume that multiplying a matrix G1 of dimension pxq with another matrix G2 of
dimension pxq requires pqr scalar multiplications. Computing the product of n  matrices G1G2G3...Gn can be done by parenthesizing in different ways. Define Gi Gi+1 as an explicitly computed pair for a given paranthesization if they are directly multiplied. For example, in the matrix multiplication chain G1G2G3G4G5G6 using parenthesization (G1(G2G3))(G4(G5G6)), G2G3 and G5G6 are the only explicitly computed pairs. Consider a matrix multiplication chain F1F2F3F4F5, where matrices F1, F2, F3, F4 and F5 are of dimensions 2x25, 25x3, 3x16, 16x1 and 1x1000, respectively. In the parenthesization of F1F2F3F4F5 that minimizes the total number of scalar multiplications, the explicitly computed pairs is/are
questions.solution:
Dimensions 2, 25, 3, 16, 1, 1000. Because [latex]F_4[/latex] has 1 column, it pays to collapse [latex]F_1..F_4[/latex] into a 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 matrix first, then multiply by [latex]F_5[/latex]:
[latex]F_3F_4[/latex]: 48 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]F_2(F_3F_4)[/latex]: 75 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]F_1(\ldots)[/latex]: 50 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex](\ldots)F_5[/latex]: 2000. Total 2173, the minimum.

The only pair of original matrices multiplied directly is [latex]F_3F_4[/latex].

Answer: F3F4 only

questions.text:
Let G be a simple undirected graph. Let TD be a depth first search tree of G. Let TB be a breadth first search tree of G. Consider the following statements.

(I) No edge of G is a cross edge with respect to TD. (A cross edge in G is between two nodes neither of which is an ancestor of the other in TD.)
(II) For every edge (u,v) of G, if u is at depth i and v is at depth j in TB, then |i-j|=1.

Which of the statements above must necessarily be true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- (I): in DFS of an undirected graph, every non-tree edge joins a vertex to its ancestor (back edge); cross edges cannot occur True
- (II): in BFS, an edge can join two vertices at the same depth (e.g. a triangle), so |i [latex]-[/latex] j| can be 0 False

Answer: I only

questions.text: Which of the following algorithms solves the all pair shortest path problem?
questions.solution:
Floyd-Warshall computes shortest paths between all pairs of vertices in [latex]O(n^3)[/latex]. Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford are single-source; Prim builds an MST.

Answer: Floyd warshalls algorithm

questions.text: The number of swappings needed to sort the numbers 8 , 22, 7, 9, 31, 5, 13 in ascending order using bubble sort is
questions.solution:
Bubble sort swaps once for each inversion (pair in the wrong order):
8 [latex]\gt[/latex] 7, 5 (2); 22 [latex]\gt[/latex] 7, 9, 5, 13 (4); 7 [latex]\gt[/latex] 5 (1); 9 [latex]\gt[/latex] 5 (1); 31 [latex]\gt[/latex] 5, 13 (2)

Total = 2 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 10

Answer: 10

questions.text: Which one of the following in-place sorting algorithms needs the minimum number of swaps?
questions.solution:
Selection sort makes at most one swap per pass, i.e. at most n [latex]-[/latex] 1 swaps in total, which is the fewest among these in-place sorts.

Answer: Selection Sort
